notes: Fiscal year ended December 31, 2024 (matches data.js fy 'Dec 2024'). Ford's 10-K columns run 2022, 2023, 2024 (left to right). HENRY FORD: deceased founder, so pctEconomic is null. FAMILY: the 2025 proxy (filed March 28, 2025) lists a voting trust with 70,778,212 Class B shares (99.90% of Class B) as of February 1, 2025. Its trustees are Edsel B. Ford II, William Clay Ford, Jr., Benson Ford, Jr. and Alfred B. Ford. The proxy names William Clay Ford, Jr. as a Ford family member and refers to 'the Ford family's more than 121 years of active involvement with and stewardship of the Company'. Holders of Class B Stock together have 40% of the general voting power. The proxy gives no percentage of all shares for the trust, so family.pctEconomic is null rather than derived. For reference, the trust's 70,778,212 Class B shares compare with 3,905,695,396 common plus 70,852,076 Class B shares outstanding at March 12, 2025. Individual Class B holders listed in the proxy (Edsel B. Ford II 6.62%, Lynn F. Alandt 9.05%, David P. Larsen as trustee 14.73%) are not added, because they overlap the voting trust's total. Ford family directors' own common-stock holdings are not added either. HOLDERS: percentages are of common stock only (Class B is under 2% of all shares). The proxy says that as of December 31, 2024 these entities had more than 5%, but the share counts come from Schedules 13G/A with these event dates: Vanguard, 12/31/2024 (filed January 8, 2025: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37996/000093247125000033/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X01/primary_doc.xml); State Street, 12/31/2023 (filed January 29, 2024: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37996/000009375124000310/Ford_Motor_Co.txt); BlackRock, December 31, 2023 (filed January 26, 2024: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/37996/000108636424004592/us3453708600_012624.txt). State Street's 8.38% includes the 4.47% it holds as trustee of the Ford defined contribution plans master trust, which is held for employees. DIVIDENDS are payments on Common and Class B Stock, including dividend equivalents; 2024 included a $0.18 supplemental dividend. PLAN: null; no broad employee stock purchase plan is described in the 10-K. STOCK COMP: the cash-flow add-back of $511m is pre-tax; Note 6 reports RSU/RSS compensation cost of $411m net of a $100m tax benefit.

footprint.notes: Ford publishes no state-by-state jobs or investment table that was found. Its corporate.ford.com Global Offices & Plants page lists each plant with approximate employees (U.S. plants marked "Headcount data from June 2026", newer than the snapshot; others undated); per-state totals are not derived from it, so selected plants appear as sites. The 10-K gives ~171,000 employees worldwide with no regional split, says Ford and consolidated entities use over 375 operations facilities across 24 countries and 41 manufacturing and assembly plants, and names joint-venture plants (China, Türkiye, Romania, Thailand, BlueOval SK battery plants in Tennessee and Kentucky) without counts. Ford From the Road (company-published) says approximately 57,000 hourly U.S. manufacturing workers at year-end 2024 (10-K: ~56,500 UAW-represented). Ford's corporate economic-impact page (corporate.ford.com/social-impact/economic-impact.html) returned only site navigation in its static HTML, so its body could not be read; no state-level U.S. investment figures were found on the Ford pages that could be read. Long-lived assets by country: U.S., Canada, UK, Mexico and All Other.
